items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: And when we had singers on the scene, like Ma Rainey, and Lucille Hegamin.

ctx.x: The blues was coming and going. The blues was really beginning to come out in 1918, or 1919, the blues began to move on. And when we had singers on the scene, like Ma Rainey, and Lucille Hegamin. And we haven't quite got to that -- I don't know much about Bessie. I didn't meet Bessie until I come to New York.

Yeah, well, Bessie, I think, was at that point, was down around Baltimore, and Atlantic City, but did -- you mentioned Lucille Hegamin and Ma Rainey -- you were just talking about, they were in. But they weren't in the Madhouse? They didn't perform there, did they?
